children.why_this_cut: Covers the first three sections (Be clear and direct, Be suitably professional, Have conversational sense). The only crossing linkage is the style_section_authority concept (heading tags assign authority=guideline or authority=user), which is seeded and applies to all sections in this span; no other concept crosses into the later sections.

Covers the remaining sections (Be warm, Don't make unprompted personal comments, Avoid being condescending or patronizing, When appropriate be helpful when refusing). The only crossing linkage is the style_section_authority concept, which is seeded and applies to all sections in this span; no other concept crosses into the earlier sections.

seed_vocabulary.name: style_section_authority
seed_vocabulary.prose: the authority level assigned to each style section by its heading tag (authority=user or authority=guideline), which determines how the section's rules rank in the chain of command

seed_vocabulary.name: refusal_style
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of being helpful when refusing, typically 'Safe Completing' by briefly explaining why it cannot provide a full answer and then doing its best to provide safe and useful assistance

seed_vocabulary.name: stay_in_bounds_section
seed_vocabulary.prose: the section of the Model Spec describing limits on the assistant's behavior, including scenarios where it should refrain from fully complying with a user or developer request

seed_vocabulary.name: risky_situations
seed_vocabulary.prose: the section providing instructions for handling requests that involve risky situations (imminent harm, illicit behavior, self-harm, regulated advice, mental health)

seed_vocabulary.name: avoid_errors
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of avoiding factual, reasoning, and formatting errors that would compromise the accuracy or utility of responses

seed_vocabulary.name: hidden_chain_of_thought
seed_vocabulary.prose: a hidden chain-of-thought message used to reason before generating a final answer, not exposed to the user or developer except in summarized form

seed_vocabulary.name: assume_best_intentions
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of applying three implicit biases (average reasonable human goals, positive intent, weak preference for self-actualization/kindness/truth/flourishing) when interpreting ambiguous instructions

seed_vocabulary.name: prohibited_content
seed_vocabulary.prose: content that should never be produced by the assistant in any circumstance, including transformations of user-provided content; only sexual content involving minors is prohibited

seed_vocabulary.name: restricted_content
seed_vocabulary.prose: content the assistant must not generate except in specific cases involving transformation of user-provided content; includes information hazards and sensitive personal data

judgment_calls: Chose a 2-way split at L3953 (between Have conversational sense and Be warm) rather than a 3-way split, because the first three sections form a cohesive block of conversational style rules and the last five form a block of tone/refusal rules; a 3-way split would have required more cross-links without a cleaner cut.

The expected_cross_links list includes several entries that are actually dangling needs for a single child (e.g., refusal_style, stay_in_bounds_section, risky_situations, avoid_errors, hidden_chain_of_thought, assume_best_intentions, prohibited_content, restricted_content) rather than true cross-child links; I included them to document that these concepts are needed by one child and provided by neither child, so they will remain dangling for the parent to resolve.

I carried all inherited seeds that appear anywhere in my span (style_section_authority, refusal_style, stay_in_bounds_section, risky_situations, avoid_errors, hidden_chain_of_thought, assume_best_intentions, prohibited_content, restricted_content) even though most are only needed by one child, because dropping them would lose the names for the whole subtree.
